# Business Law and Practice: what is examined {#sec-blp-overview}

## Assessment objectives

Candidates are required to apply relevant core legal principles and rules appropriately and
effectively, at the level of a competent newly qualified solicitor in practice, to realistic
client-based and ethical problems and situations in the following areas:

1. Starting a new business through the vehicle of a company, partnership, LLP or as a sole trader.
2. The management of a business and company decision making to ensure compliance with statutory and
   other legal requirements.
3. The interests, rights, obligations and powers of stakeholders in a business.
4. Financing a business.
5. Taxation of a business and its stakeholders.
6. The termination of a solvent business, corporate insolvency and personal bankruptcy.

Candidates must demonstrate their ability to act honestly and with integrity and in accordance with
the Statement of Solicitor Competence, the SRA Principles and the Code of Conduct.

Questions may draw on any combination of the subject areas within FLK1.

## How this part is organised

Each of the six objectives gets a chapter, in the order the SRA lists them. That ordering is not
accidental: it follows the life of a business, and the later chapters assume the earlier ones.

| Objective | Chapter |
|---|---|
| 1. Starting a business | @sec-blp-vehicles — Choosing and forming the vehicle |
| 2. Management and compliance | @sec-blp-management — Running the business |
| 3. Stakeholders | @sec-blp-stakeholders — Rights, powers and protection |
| 4. Financing | @sec-blp-finance — Equity, debt and distributions |
| 5. Taxation | @sec-blp-taxation — The five taxes |
| 6. Termination | @sec-blp-termination — Solvent exit and insolvency |

## Two warnings before you start

**This subject is disproportionately large.** Business Law and Practice is the biggest single
subject in FLK1 and carries five taxes inside it. Candidates routinely underestimate the tax
component because it sits at the end of the specification and looks like an appendix. It is not.

**The questions cross subjects.** The specification says explicitly that questions may combine
areas encountered in practice. A company law scenario can turn on contract formation, on a
solicitor's conflict of interest, or on whether a floating charge crystallised. Learning this
subject in isolation from the rest of FLK1 will leave you exposed to precisely the questions the
examiner finds most attractive.
